claim: 2BAct is a highly selective eIF2B activator with an EC50 of 33 nM in a cell-based ISR attenuation reporter assay.
source: 2BAct is a highly selective eIF2B activator and exhibited similar potency to ISRIB in a cell-based reporter assay that measures ISR attenuation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from a cell-based reporter assay shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, with the EC50 value explicitly stated.

claim: 2BAct can penetrate the central nervous system with an unbound brain/plasma ratio of approximately 0.3.
source: 2BAct is able to penetrate the central nervous system (CNS) (unbound brain/plasma ratio ~0.3)
evidence: The claim is supported by pharmacokinetic data measuring brain and plasma concentrations of 2BAct.

claim: 2BAct demonstrated dose-dependent oral bioavailability using an aqueous-based vehicle.
source: 2BAct is able to penetrate the central nervous system (CNS) (unbound brain/plasma ratio ~0.3) and also demonstrated dose-dependent oral bioavailability using an aqueous-based vehicle (Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by pharmacokinetic data presented in Supplementary file 1B.

claim: 2BAct is well-suited for formulation in diet and does not affect body weight in WT mice during long-term dosing.
source: Additionally, 2BAct is well-suited for formulation in diet, enabling long-term dosing without effects on body weight in WT mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by body weight measurements in WT mice treated with 2BAct shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 2BAct was well-tolerated in the animal studies described but showed significant cardiovascular anomalies in a dog CV model, making it unsuitable for human dosing.
source: The molecule was well-tolerated in the animal studies described here, and did not elicit any relevant effects in a rat cardiovascular (CV) safety study; however, significant anomalies were observed in a dog CV model. This CV safety liability makes this particular molecule unsuitable for human dosing.
evidence: The claim is supported by cardiovascular safety study data in rats and dogs.

claim: R191H mice have significantly reduced GEF activity compared to WT mice.
source: We confirmed that primary fibroblast lysates from R191H embryos had lower GEF activity than WT lysates, and that 2BAct enhanced this activity threefold (EC50 = 7.3 nM; Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by GEF assay data comparing WT and R191H mouse embryonic fibroblast lysates shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: 2BAct enhanced the GEF activity of R191H lysates threefold with an EC50 of 7.3 nM.
source: We confirmed that primary fibroblast lysates from R191H embryos had lower GEF activity than WT lysates, and that 2BAct enhanced this activity threefold (EC50 = 7.3 nM; Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by dose-response GEF assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: At 6-11 weeks of age, WT and R191H male mice had similar body weights.
source: At the initiation of the study (6–11 weeks old), WT and R191H males had similar body weights (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by body weight measurements shown in Figure 1C.

claim: One week after the start of the study, R191H mice showed significantly lower body weight compared to WT mice, and this difference continued to grow.
source: However, 1 week later, a significant difference emerged and continued to grow as R191H mice failed to gain weight (WT gain = 0.5 g/week vs. R191H gain = 0.08 g/week; p<10−4).
evidence: The claim is supported by longitudinal body weight measurements with statistical analysis.

claim: 2BAct-treated R191H males caught up to WT mice body weight 2 weeks after beginning dosing (8-13 weeks old).
source: Remarkably, the body weight of 2BAct-treated R191H males caught up to WT mice 2 weeks after beginning dosing (8–13 weeks old), at which point their rate of weight gain equalized (WT gain = 0.5 g/week vs. R191H gain = 0.55 g/week; p = 0.24; Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by body weight measurements and statistical analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: R191H mice showed no significant difference from WT in inverted grid test performance from 8 to 19 weeks of age.
source: From 8 to 19 weeks of age, R191H animals were not significantly different from WT in their performance on an inverted grid test of neuromuscular function.
evidence: The claim is supported by inverted grid test data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: At 23 weeks, R191H mice showed a trend towards shorter hang times in the inverted grid test, and at 26 weeks, this decrease was highly significant in both sexes.
source: At 23 weeks, R191H mice showed a trend towards shorter hang times and at 26 weeks, this decrease was highly significant in both sexes (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by inverted grid test data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: R191H mice were not significantly different from WT littermates in beam-crossing test at 8-19 weeks of age.
source: In a beam-crossing test of balance and motor coordination, R191H mice were not significantly different from WT littermates at 8–19 weeks of age (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by beam-crossing test data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C-D.

claim: At 23 weeks of age, R191H mice showed significantly increased beam-crossing time and exhibited more foot slips and falls from the beam.
source: However, at 23 weeks of age, beam-crossing time was significantly increased in mutant animals, and they exhibited more foot slips and falls from the beam while crossing.
evidence: The claim is supported by beam-crossing test data with statistical analysis.

claim: The motor coordination deficit in R191H mice was exacerbated at 26 weeks, with some animals completely failing to cross the beam within the trial cutoff of 30 seconds.
source: The deficit in both parameters was exacerbated at 26 weeks, and some R191H animals completely failed to cross the beam within the trial cutoff of 30 s (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by beam-crossing test data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Placebo-treated R191H males had significantly reduced inverted grid hang times at both tested time points.
source: Placebo-treated R191H males had significantly reduced inverted grid hang times at both tested time points, as well as more coordination errors and time spent crossing the balance beam (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by inverted grid test data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: 2BAct-treated R191H males were indistinguishable from WT in both inverted grid and beam-crossing assays.
source: By contrast, 2BAct-treated R191H males were indistinguishable from WT in both assays.
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral test data shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: Full normalization of motor function by 2BAct was similarly observed in female animals.
source: Full normalization was similarly observed in female animals (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by behavioral test data in female mice shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4B-D.

claim: R191H animals showed a 33% reduction in myelin in the corpus callosum compared to WT (p<10−4).
source: As anticipated, R191H animals showed a clear reduction in myelin by Luxol Fast Blue staining of both regions (33% reduction in corpus callosum, p<10−4; 58% reduction in cervical/thoracic spinal cord, p<10−4; Figure 2A–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Luxol Fast Blue staining quantification shown in Figure 2A-B.

claim: R191H animals showed a 58% reduction in myelin in the cervical/thoracic spinal cord compared to WT (p<10−4).
source: As anticipated, R191H animals showed a clear reduction in myelin by Luxol Fast Blue staining of both regions (33% reduction in corpus callosum, p<10−4; 58% reduction in cervical/thoracic spinal cord, p<10−4; Figure 2A–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Luxol Fast Blue staining quantification shown in Figure 2C-D.

claim: 2BAct treatment maintained myelin levels at 91% of WT in the corpus callosum and 85% of WT in the spinal cord.
source: Strikingly, 2BAct treatment maintained myelin levels at 91% and 85% of WT in the corpus callosum and spinal cord, respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by Luxol Fast Blue staining quantification data.

claim: Staining for myelin basic protein (MBP) corroborated the Luxol Fast Blue results in both corpus callosum and spinal cord.
source: Staining for myelin basic protein (MBP), an alternative measure of myelin content, corroborated these results in both regions (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by MBP immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-D.

claim: There was a significant increase in GFAP in both corpus callosum and spinal cord of placebo-treated R191H mice, which was fully normalized by 2BAct treatment.
source: We found a significant increase in GFAP in both regions of placebo-treated R191H mice, which was fully normalized by 2BAct treatment (Figure 2A–B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by GFAP immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2A-B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: There was a significant increase in Olig2 in R191H spinal cord.
source: Consistent with the literature, we noted a significant increase in Olig2 in R191H spinal cord (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Olig2 immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: Olig2 is a marker of the oligodendrocyte lineage, and its increase could indicate an attempt to compensate for myelin loss.
source: Olig2 is a marker of the oligodendrocyte lineage, and its increase could indicate an attempt to compensate for the myelin loss (Bugiani et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is based on interpretation of Olig2 data in the context of cited literature.

claim: There was a 15-fold increase in Iba-1 staining in placebo-treated R191H spinal cord samples, indicating reactive microglia.
source: Additionally, we observed signs of reactive microglia in the placebo-treated R191H samples, as evidenced by a 15-fold increase in Iba-1 staining (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Iba-1 immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2C-D.

claim: ATF3 was significantly increased in R191H spinal cord.
source: ATF3, an ISR target induced in the spinal cord during injury and inflammation, was also significantly increased (Dominguez et al., 2010; Hossain-Ibrahim et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by ATF3 immunohistochemistry data and cited literature on ATF3 function.

claim: 2BAct treatment fully normalized Olig2, Iba-1, and ATF3 markers in R191H spinal cord.
source: 2BAct treatment fully normalized all four of these markers (Figure 2C–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2C-D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: At 2 months of age, there were no significant differences in myelin, Iba-1, or ATF3 between R191H and WT spinal cord.
source: In an analysis of younger mice, we observed no significant differences in myelin, Iba-1 or ATF3 between R191H and WT spinal cord at the start of treatment (2 months of age; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis at 2 months of age shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The time course of pathology was consistent with the emergence of motor deficits and reflected the degenerative nature of VWM.
source: The time course of pathology was consistent with the emergence of motor deficits, and reflected the degenerative nature of VWM.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the temporal correlation between histological and behavioral data.

claim: The ISR was robustly and consistently induced at 2.5, 5, and 7 months in the cerebellum, forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain of R191H animals.
source: The ISR was robustly and consistently induced at these time points in the cerebellum, forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain of R191H animals (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by mRNA expression data of ISR target genes shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Significant upregulation of all ISR targets except Gadd34, Slc1a5 and Gadd45a was evident in cerebellum at 2.5 months.
source: Significant upregulation of all targets except Gadd34, Slc1a5 and Gadd45a was evident in cerebellum at 2.5 months; at later timepoints, these three transcripts also became significantly induced.
evidence: The claim is supported by mRNA expression data at different time points.

claim: Atf5, Eif4ebp1 and Trib3 were the most upregulated transcripts in the ISR panel across all brain regions.
source: The ISR signature was similar across all brain regions with Atf5, Eif4ebp1 and Trib3 being the most upregulated transcripts in the panel.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparative analysis of mRNA expression data across brain regions.

claim: ISR induction was not observed in R191H mice at postnatal day 14.
source: Interestingly, we did not observe ISR induction in R191H mice at postnatal day 14 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by mRNA expression data at postnatal day 14 shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The ISR is activated sometime between 2 and 8 weeks of age through an as-yet unknown mechanism.
source: Thus, the ISR is activated sometime between 2 and 8 weeks of age through an as-yet unknown mechanism.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the temporal pattern of ISR activation observed in the data.

claim: Activation of the ISR preceded the appearance of pathology (myelin loss, gliosis and motor deficits) in VWM mice.
source: Activation of this stress response preceded the appearance of pathology (myelin loss, gliosis and motor deficits) in VWM mice.
evidence: The claim is based on temporal comparison of ISR activation and pathological phenotypes.

claim: Translational induction of ATF4 and increased protein levels of EIF4EBP1 were confirmed by Western blot analysis of 7-month-old R191H cerebellum lysates.
source: In addition to changes in transcript levels, we confirmed translational induction of ATF4 as well as the increase in protein levels of the negative regulator of cap-mediated mRNA translation EIF4EBP1 by Western blot analysis of 7-month-old R191H cerebellum lysates (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: No increase in eIF2α phosphorylation was detected in R191H brains.
source: As expected for an ISR induced by eIF2B dysfunction rather than external stressors (see schematic in Figure 3C), we did not detect an increase in eIF2α phosphorylation in R191H brains.
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data and is consistent with the mechanism of eIF2B dysfunction.

claim: Greater ISR induction was observed in the spinal cord compared to the cerebellum.
source: We observed greater ISR induction in the spinal cord compared to the cerebellum (Figure 3D, compare red and brown points), with the transcription factor Atf3 showing an additional 10-fold increase.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparative mRNA expression data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Treatment with 2BAct abolished ISR induction in both cerebellum and spinal cord.
source: Notably, treatment with 2BAct abolished ISR induction in both regions (Figure 3B,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by mRNA and protein expression data shown in Figure 3B and 3D.

claim: Significant upregulation of Atf5 and Eif4ebp1 was detected in Eif2b5R132H/R132H mice, which was blocked by 4 weeks of treatment with 2BAct.
source: Nevertheless, we detected significant upregulation of two ISR targets, Atf5 and Eif4ebp1, that was blocked by 4 weeks of treatment with 2BAct (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by mRNA expression data in the R132H mouse model shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Upregulation of ATF4 targets was not detected in skeletal muscle, liver, kidney or ovaries of R191H mice.
source: Upregulation of ATF4 targets was not detected in skeletal muscle, liver, kidney or ovaries (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), demonstrating that the CNS is particularly sensitive to a reduction in eIF2B function.
evidence: The claim is supported by mRNA expression data in peripheral tissues shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The CNS is particularly sensitive to a reduction in eIF2B function.
source: Upregulation of ATF4 targets was not detected in skeletal muscle, liver, kidney or ovaries (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), demonstrating that the CNS is particularly sensitive to a reduction in eIF2B function.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the tissue-specific pattern of ISR activation.

claim: Upregulation of ISR target genes was confirmed in R191H cerebellum beginning as early as 2 months of age, with sustained magnitude at 5 and 7 months.
source: We confirmed the upregulation of ISR target genes beginning as early as 2 months of age, the magnitude of which was sustained at 5 and 7 months (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: No changes in expression were observed for known downstream targets of the IRE1α or ATF6-dependent branches of the unfolded protein response at any time point.
source: By contrast, and as expected for a disease driven by dysfunction in eIF2B, we did not observe changes in expression for known downstream targets of the parallel IRE1α or ATF6-dependent branches of the unfolded protein response at any time point (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-C and is consistent with the mechanism of disease.

claim: 473 genes with increased expression in R191H mice were identified by SVD analysis of 2-month-old cerebellum.
source: The first class consisted of 473 genes with increased expression (positive loadings) in R191H mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by SVD analysis of RNA-seq data.

claim: GO-term enrichment analysis of upregulated genes revealed categories containing many known ATF4-dependent targets involved in amino acid metabolism and tRNA aminoacylation.
source: Unsurprisingly, GO-term enrichment analysis revealed categories that contained many known ATF4-dependent targets involved in amino acid metabolism and tRNA aminoacylation (Supplementary file 1C) (Adamson et al., 2016; Han et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by GO-term enrichment analysis of RNA-seq data and cited literature on ATF4 targets.

claim: 600 genes with reduced expression in R191H mice were identified by SVD analysis.
source: A second class comprised 600 genes with reduced expression (negative loadings).
evidence: The claim is supported by SVD analysis of RNA-seq data.

claim: GO-term enrichment analysis of downregulated genes revealed categories related to myelination and lipid metabolism.
source: These genes were not restricted to expression in a specific cell type, but GO-term enrichment analysis revealed categories related to myelination and lipid metabolism (Supplementary file 1C), suggesting an effect on glial cells such as astrocytes and oligodendrocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by GO-term enrichment analysis of RNA-seq data.

claim: A gene signature of perturbed myelin maintenance is detectable as early as 2 months, preceding evidence of myelin loss by histological analysis.
source: A gene signature of perturbed myelin maintenance is detectable as early as 2 months, preceding evidence of myelin loss by histological analysis.
evidence: The claim is based on temporal comparison of RNA-seq and histological data.

claim: Both upregulated and downregulated classes of transcripts were normalized in 2BAct-treated R191H mice.
source: Remarkably, both upregulated and downregulated classes of transcripts were normalized in 2BAct-treated R191H mice (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Clustering of samples based on the top 50 genes confirmed that 2BAct-treated R191H mice were indistinguishable from WT.
source: Clustering of samples based on the top 50 genes from the previous analysis confirmed that 2BAct-treated R191H mice were indistinguishable from WT (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: 2BAct treatment of WT mice did not significantly alter gene expression compared to placebo.
source: Moreover, 2BAct treatment of WT mice did not significantly alter gene expression compared to placebo (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data comparing 2BAct-treated and placebo-treated WT mice shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-B.

claim: Unbiased clustering of single cells from forebrain and cerebellum identified 13 and 10 clusters, respectively.
source: Unbiased clustering of single cells from each region identified 13 and 10 clusters in the forebrain and cerebellum, respectively, that were subsequently assigned cell type identities using CNS cell type gene markers obtained from bulk RNA-seq data (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A) (Koirala and Corfas, 2010; Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq clustering analysis shown in Figure 5A and supplementary figures.

claim: Cells from both WT and R191H tissues were represented in each cluster, demonstrating that transcriptionally defined cell types are not influenced by genotype at 2.5 months.
source: Cells from both WT and R191H tissues were represented in each cluster, demonstrating that transcriptionally defined cell types are not influenced by genotype at this early time point in disease progression.
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq clustering analysis showing mixed genotype representation.

claim: CLIC analysis identified 18 of the input genes as coherently co-expressed across 1774 diverse mouse microarray datasets and expanded this co-expression module to a final signature comprising 95 genes.
source: CLIC identified 18 of our input genes as coherently co-expressed across 1774 diverse mouse microarray datasets, and expanded this co-expression module to a final signature comprising 95 genes (Supplementary file 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by CLIC analysis results.

claim: Two astrocyte clusters in the forebrain and Bergmann glia in the cerebellum showed significant enrichment of the ISR signature in WT cells.
source: Strikingly, two astrocyte clusters in the forebrain and Bergmann glia in the cerebellum showed significant enrichment of the ISR signature (q = 0.004, 0.008 and 0.004, respectively), indicating that these cell types have higher basal expression of ISR targets (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis of scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The ISR signature was insignificant or negatively enriched in other WT CNS cell types.
source: By contrast, the ISR signature was insignificant (using a threshold of q = 0.05) or even negatively enriched in other WT CNS cell types.
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis of scRNA-seq data.

claim: In the forebrain, the two astrocyte clusters with an enriched ISR signature in WT showed significant further upregulation in R191H tissue (q < 10−3 for both clusters).
source: In the forebrain, the two astrocyte clusters with an enriched ISR signature in WT showed significant further upregulation in R191H tissue (q < 10−3 for both clusters; Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis of scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Bergmann glia showed the most significant enrichment of the ISR signature in R191H cerebellum tissue (q = 0.0004).
source: In the cerebellum, Bergmann glia also showed the most significant enrichment of the ISR signature in R191H tissue (q = 0.0004; Figure 5—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis of scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Astrocytes and Bergmann glia have long been implicated as the affected cell type in VWM based on histology and ex vivo analyses.
source: Astrocytes, and more recently Bergmann glia, have long been implicated as the affected cell type in VWM based on histology and ex vivo analyses (Bugiani et al., 2011; Dietrich et al., 2005; Dooves et al., 2016; Dooves et al., 2018; Geva et al., 2010; Leferink et al., 2018; Wong et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple cited studies on VWM pathology.

claim: This work provides the first in vivo evidence that in VWM mice, astrocytes exhibit a molecular signature of an early maladaptive ISR.
source: For the first time, our work provides in vivo evidence that in VWM mice, astrocytes exhibit a molecular signature of an early maladaptive ISR.
evidence: The claim is based on the scRNA-seq data showing ISR activation in astrocytes.

claim: The comparison of R191H to WT cerebellum revealed significant enrichment of the ISR signature in myelinating oligodendrocytes, an unassigned cell type, and endothelial cells (q = 0.001, 0.005 and 0.02, respectively).
source: Interestingly, the comparison of R191H to WT cerebellum also revealed significant enrichment of the ISR signature in other non-neuronal cell types, including myelinating oligodendrocytes, an unassigned cell type, and endothelial cells (q = 0.001, 0.005 and 0.02, respectively; Figure 5—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis of scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2C.

claim: 42 proteins increased >1.5 fold in abundance and 19 proteins decreased >1.5 fold in abundance in placebo-treated R191H vs. WT at a posterior probability >90%.
source: We discovered 42 proteins that increased >1.5 fold in abundance, and 19 proteins that decreased >1.5 fold in abundance in placebo-treated R191H vs. WT at a posterior probability >90% (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by TMT-MS proteomics data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Of the upregulated proteins, 21/42 were transcriptionally upregulated in the RNA-seq experiment.
source: Of the upregulated proteins, 21/42 were transcriptionally upregulated in the RNA-seq experiment.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of proteomics and RNA-seq data.

claim: TMT-MS did not detect ATF4 or some of its low-abundance targets (e.g. the transcription factors ATF3, ATF5 and CHOP).
source: However, TMT-MS did not detect ATF4 or some of its low-abundance targets (e.g. the transcription factors ATF3, ATF5 and CHOP).
evidence: The claim is based on the absence of certain proteins in the proteomics dataset.

claim: Of the downregulated proteins, 13/19 were transcriptionally downregulated in the RNA-seq experiment.
source: Of the downregulated proteins, 13/19 were transcriptionally downregulated in the RNA-seq experiment, one did not change transcriptionally and five did not meet the RNA-seq abundance threshold.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of proteomics and RNA-seq data.

claim: 14/19 of the downregulated proteins are most highly expressed in Bergmann glia or astrocytes, and 9/19 are highly expressed in oligodendrocytes or oligodendrocyte precursor cells.
source: Remarkably, 14/19 of these targets are most highly expressed in Bergmann glia or astrocytes, and 9/19 are highly expressed in oligodendroyctes or oligodendrocyte precursor cells (Tabula Muris Consortium et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of proteomics data with published cell type expression data.

claim: All downregulated proteins and 40/42 upregulated proteins were normalized by 2BAct treatment.
source: Importantly, all downregulated proteins and 40/42 upregulated proteins were normalized by 2BAct treatment (Figure 6A right panel and Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomics data comparing 2BAct-treated and placebo-treated R191H mice shown in Figure 6A and 6C.

claim: Levels of all five eIF2B subunits were reduced 15-35% in R191H cerebellum compared to WT.
source: Interestingly, we discovered that levels of all five eIF2B subunits were reduced 15–35% in R191H cerebellum compared to WT (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomics data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The decrease in eIF2B subunit levels occurred at the protein level, as no changes were observed in transcript abundance by RNA-seq.
source: This decrease occurred at the protein level, as no changes were observed in transcript abundance by RNA-seq.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of proteomics and RNA-seq data.

claim: Long-term treatment with 2BAct does not rescue eIF2B complex levels in vivo.
source: The finding that long-term treatment with 2BAct does not rescue eIF2B complex levels in vivo suggests that the normalization of all measured endpoints in R191H mice (Table 1) is due to boosting the GEF activity of the remaining mutant complex to functionally normal levels.
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomics data showing no change in eIF2B levels with 2BAct treatment.

claim: The normalization of all measured endpoints in R191H mice is due to boosting the GEF activity of the remaining mutant complex to functionally normal levels.
source: The finding that long-term treatment with 2BAct does not rescue eIF2B complex levels in vivo suggests that the normalization of all measured endpoints in R191H mice (Table 1) is due to boosting the GEF activity of the remaining mutant complex to functionally normal levels.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation that 2BAct normalizes phenotypes without increasing eIF2B levels.

claim: Introduction of a severe VWM mutation into mice led to spontaneous loss of myelin and motor deficits that reproduce key aspects of the human disease.
source: Introduction of a severe VWM mutation into mice led to spontaneous loss of myelin and motor deficits that reproduce key aspects of the human disease.
evidence: The claim is supported by the comprehensive characterization of the R191H mouse model.

claim: The impaired GEF activity of mutant eIF2B underlies the observed translational upregulation of ATF4 and induction of a maladaptive ISR program that precedes behavioral pathology.
source: The impaired GEF activity of mutant eIF2B underlies the observed translational upregulation of the transcription factor ATF4 and in turn, induction of a maladaptive ISR program that precedes behavioral pathology.
evidence: The claim is based on the temporal relationship between ISR activation and pathology, combined with mechanistic understanding of eIF2B function.

claim: A subset of astrocytes possess a basal ISR in normal mice, which is further activated when eIF2B is mutated.
source: Our data demonstrate that a subset of astrocytes possess a basal ISR in normal mice, which is further activated when eIF2B is mutated.
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq data showing ISR enrichment in astrocyte clusters in both WT and R191H mice.

claim: ISR upregulation was detected in other non-neuronal cell populations, including myelinating oligodendrocytes.
source: Notably, we also detected ISR upregulation in other non-neuronal cell populations, including myelinating oligodendrocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by scRNA-seq data showing ISR enrichment in multiple cell types.

claim: White matter astrocytes, but not grey matter astrocytes, are dysmorphic in VWM patients.
source: Histological analysis has shown that white matter astrocytes, but not grey matter astrocytes, are dysmorphic and a subset of oligodendrocytes are characterized as foamy in VWM patients (Hata et al., 2014; Wong et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited histological studies of VWM patients.

claim: Bergman glia and Muller glia were shown to be severely affected in patients and in VWM mouse models.
source: Moreover, Bergman glia, astrocytes found in the cerebellum, and Muller glia, astrocytes found in the retina, were shown to be severely affected in patients and in VWM mouse models (Dooves et al., 2016; Dooves et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited studies on VWM pathology.

claim: Cellular and metabolic dysfunction in astrocytes could lead to malfunction in other cell types such as the myelinating oligodendrocytes.
source: As cells in the brain are highly interconnected, cellular and metabolic dysfunction in astrocytes could lead to malfunction in other cell types such as the myelinating oligodendrocytes.
evidence: The claim is based on speculation about cellular interactions in the brain.

claim: Whether ISR activation in the non-astrocytic cells is cell-autonomous or triggered by signals from astrocytes remains to be explored.
source: Whether ISR activation in the non-astrocytic cells is cell-autonomous or triggered by signals from astrocytes remains to be explored.
evidence: The claim acknowledges an unanswered question about the mechanism of ISR activation in different cell types.

claim: ATF4 is chronically induced in various mouse models of mitochondrial dysfunction.
source: Interestingly, ATF4 is chronically induced in various mouse models of mitochondrial dysfunction, and mutations in human mitochondrial proteins can lead to loss of myelin or leukoencephalopathies (Carvalho, 2013; Dogan et al., 2014; Huang et al., 2013; Mendes et al., 2018; Moisoi et al., 2009; Pereira et al., 2017; Quirós et al., 2017; Taylor et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple cited studies on mitochondrial dysfunction and ATF4.

claim: The induction of Eif4ebp1 and Sesn2 suggests that impairment of translation in VWM may extend beyond the direct effect of crippled eIF2B activity.
source: The induction of Eif4ebp1 and Sesn2, two negative regulators of the mTOR signaling pathway, suggests that impairment of translation in VWM may extend beyond the direct effect of crippled eIF2B activity (Budanov and Karin, 2008; Wolfson et al., 2016; Yanagiya et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the upregulation of mTOR pathway inhibitors and cited literature on their function.

claim: If protein synthesis is globally reduced by chronic ISR activation in oligodendrocytes, this could directly disrupt maintenance of the myelin sheath.
source: If protein synthesis is globally reduced by chronic ISR activation in oligodendrocytes, this could directly disrupt maintenance of the myelin sheath.
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing a mechanism for myelin loss based on ISR activation in oligodendrocytes.

claim: The ISR signature of VWM mice is unique as it originates downstream of the canonical sensor, that is eIF2α phosphorylation by stress-responsive kinases.
source: The ISR signature of VWM mice is unique as it originates downstream of the canonical sensor, that is eIF2α phosphorylation by stress-responsive kinases.
evidence: The claim is based on the mechanistic understanding that VWM mutations affect eIF2B directly rather than through eIF2α phosphorylation.

claim: In contrast to ISR induction via stress-responsive kinases, the negative feedback loop elicited by CREP and GADD34 phosphatases is not effective in attenuating the response in VWM.
source: In contrast to ISR induction via stress-responsive kinases, the negative feedback loop elicited by both the constitutive CREP-containing and the ISR-inducible GADD34-containing eIF2α phosphatases is not effective in attenuating the response in VWM.
evidence: The claim is based on the mechanistic understanding that the feedback loop operates through eIF2α dephosphorylation, which is not the primary defect in VWM.

claim: VWM constitutes a 'locked-on' ISR.
source: Therefore, it constitutes a 'locked-on' ISR (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the mechanism of ISR activation in VWM and the ineffectiveness of normal feedback mechanisms.

claim: The VWM ISR system can still respond to further stress, as seen in VWM patients wherein provoking factors exacerbate the disease.
source: However, the system can still respond to further stress, as seen in VWM patients wherein provoking factors (e.g. febrile infections or head trauma) exacerbate the disease and lead to poorer outcomes (Hamilton et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited clinical observations in VWM patients.

claim: Long-term administration of 2BAct starting at ~8 weeks of age is a preventative treatment paradigm.
source: Long-term administration of 2BAct starting at ~8 weeks of age is a preventative treatment paradigm.
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental design where treatment was initiated before the onset of pathology.

claim: Beginning treatment at later time points would likely result in ISR attenuation, as eIF2B activation by 2BAct is predicted to be age-independent.
source: Beginning treatment at later time points would likely result in ISR attenuation, as we predict that eIF2B activation by 2BAct is age-independent.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on the mechanism of action of 2BAct.

claim: The degree of pathological amelioration in a therapeutic mode would likely depend on the extent of neuronal damage and myelin perturbation at the start of treatment.
source: However, the degree of pathological amelioration in a therapeutic mode would likely depend on the extent of neuronal damage and myelin perturbation in the nervous system at the start of treatment.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on reasoning about the reversibility of accumulated damage.

claim: The remyelination capacity of humans and mice is likely to differ significantly.
source: The remyelination capacity of humans and mice is likely to differ significantly, thus the therapeutic value of eIF2B activators in VWM is best interrogated in the clinic.
evidence: The claim is based on general knowledge about species differences in regenerative capacity.

claim: ISRIB has shown beneficial effects in mouse models when administered either acutely or for short periods of time by intraperitoneal delivery.
source: Nevertheless, ISRIB has shown beneficial effects in mouse models when administered either acutely or for short periods of time by intraperitoneal delivery (Chou et al., 2017; Halliday et al., 2015; Li et al., 2018; Nguyen et al., 2018; Sidrauski et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple cited studies on ISRIB efficacy in various mouse models.

claim: The improved in vivo properties of 2BAct make it an ideal molecule to interrogate the efficacy of this mechanism of action in rodent disease models that require long-term dosing.
source: The improved in vivo properties of 2BAct make it an ideal molecule to interrogate the efficacy of this mechanism of action in rodent disease models that require long-term dosing, including those characterized by chronic activation of any of the four eIF2α kinases.
evidence: The claim is based on the demonstrated pharmacokinetic properties of 2BAct and its efficacy in the VWM model.

claim: All tested VWM mutations have responded to eIF2B activators in vitro to date.
source: To date, all tested VWM mutations have responded to eIF2B activators in vitro.
evidence: The claim is based on previous in vitro studies of VWM mutations.

claim: 2BAct increased GEF activity can compensate in vivo under conditions where a severe mutation leads to both decreased levels of eIF2B complex and reduced intrinsic activity.
source: Here, we show that increased GEF activity can compensate in vivo under conditions where a severe mutation leads to both decreased levels of eIF2B complex and reduced intrinsic activity.
evidence: The claim is supported by the comprehensive rescue of phenotypes in R191H mice despite reduced eIF2B levels.

claim: No VWM mutations are known to exist in the compound binding site of eIF2B.
source: Although it is possible to introduce artificial mutations into eIF2B that interfere with the compound binding site, no VWM mutations are known to exist in this region (Sekine et al., 2015; Tsai et al., 2018; Wong et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of known VWM mutations and the structural location of the compound binding site.

claim: 2BAct-like compounds may be broadly efficacious across the range of mutations identified in the VWM patient population.
source: Based on this, we anticipate that 2BAct-like compounds may be broadly efficacious across the range of mutations identified in the VWM patient population.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on the mechanism of action and the absence of mutations in the binding site.

claim: eIF2B activation is a sound strategy for shutting off the ISR in vivo.
source: Finally, our results demonstrate that eIF2B activation is a sound strategy for shutting off the ISR in vivo.
evidence: The claim is based on the comprehensive demonstration of ISR attenuation by 2BAct in the VWM mouse model.

claim: Various diseases exhibiting a maladaptive ISR could be responsive to eIF2B activation.
source: This raises the possibility that various diseases exhibiting a maladaptive ISR could be responsive to this mechanism of action.
evidence: The claim is speculative, extrapolating from the VWM results to other diseases with ISR activation.

claim: VWM is a rare, autosomal recessive leukodystrophy driven by mutations in eIF2B.
source: Vanishing White Matter (VWM; OMIM 603896) is a rare, autosomal recessive leukodystrophy that is driven by mutations in eIF2B (Leegwater et al., 2001; van der Knaap et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature on VWM genetics.

claim: VWM is characterized by myelin loss, progressive neurological symptoms such as ataxia, spasticity, cognitive deterioration and ultimately, death.
source: The disease is characterized by myelin loss, progressive neurological symptoms such as ataxia, spasticity, cognitive deterioration and ultimately, death (Schiffmann et al., 1994; van der Knaap et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited clinical descriptions of VWM.

claim: Age of VWM onset is variable and predictive of disease progression, ranging from severe prenatal/infantile onset to slower-progressing adult onset presentations.
source: Age of VWM onset is variable and predictive of disease progression, ranging from severe prenatal/infantile onset leading to death in months (as in the case of 'Cree leukoencephalopathy') to slower-progressing adult onset presentations (Fogli et al., 2002; Hamilton et al., 2018; van der Knaap et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited clinical studies on VWM phenotypic variability.

claim: VWM mutations are restricted to partial loss-of-function in any of the five subunits of the decameric eIF2B complex.
source: Because eIF2B is essential, VWM mutations are restricted to partial loss-of-function in any of the five subunits of the decameric complex (Fogli et al., 2004; Horzinski et al., 2009; Li et al., 2004; Liu et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited genetic studies and the essential nature of eIF2B.

claim: Nearly 200 different VWM mutations have been catalogued to date in the Human Gene Mutation Database.
source: Nearly 200 different mutations have been catalogued to date in the Human Gene Mutation Database, which occur as homozygotes or compound heterozygotes with a different mutation in each allele of the same subunit.
evidence: The claim is based on information from the Human Gene Mutation Database.

claim: Reduction of eIF2B activity is analogous to its inhibition by phosphorylated eIF2α.
source: Reduction of eIF2B activity is analogous to its inhibition by phosphorylated eIF2α, thus it is congruent and compelling that ISR activation has been observed in VWM patient post-mortem samples (van der Voorn et al., 2005; van Kollenburg et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is based on mechanistic understanding of eIF2B function and cited observations in patient samples.

claim: A range of VWM mutations destabilize the eIF2B decamer, leading to compromised GEF activity in both recombinant complexes and endogenous protein from cell lysates.
source: We previously showed that a range of VWM mutations destabilize the eIF2B decamer, leading to compromised GEF activity in both recombinant complexes and endogenous protein from cell lysates (Wong et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited previous work by the authors.

claim: ISRIB stabilized the decameric form of both wild-type and VWM mutant eIF2B complexes, boosting their intrinsic activity.
source: We demonstrated that the small molecule eIF2B activator ISRIB (for ISR inhibitor) stabilized the decameric form of both wild-type (WT) and VWM mutant complexes, boosting their intrinsic activity.
evidence: The claim is supported by cited previous work by the authors.

claim: ISRIB bridges the symmetric dimer interface of the eIF2B central core, acting as a molecular stapler.
source: Notably, ISRIB bridges the symmetric dimer interface of the eIF2B central core, acting as a molecular stapler (Tsai et al., 2018; Zyryanova et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited structural studies of ISRIB-eIF2B interaction.

claim: ISRIB attenuated ISR activation and restored protein synthesis in cells carrying VWM mutations.
source: In addition, we showed that ISRIB attenuated ISR activation and restored protein synthesis in cells carrying VWM mutations (Wong et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited previous work by the authors.

claim: The R191H mouse model recapitulates key disease phenotypes such as progressive loss of white matter with concomitant manifestation of motor deficits.
source: Knock-in mouse models of human VWM mutations have been characterized, and the severe mutations recapitulate key disease phenotypes such as progressive loss of white matter with concomitant manifestation of motor deficits (Dooves et al., 2016; Geva et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited characterizations of VWM mouse models.
